Why it is different

Five things no tourism map does

01AI connecting disciplinesGeology, archaeology and ecology read together, so one place tells one connected story.
02AI hypothesesNew, testable ideas about links between places — always labelled as untested.
03Research made accessibleScientific papers turned into illustrated stories and clear explanations, in two languages.
04Self-updating knowledgeNew discoveries are found, read and checked every week, so the map never goes stale.
05Science into journeysKnowledge becomes destinations, thematic routes and learning experiences for visitors.

Five things no tourism map does

The innovation components of LAYERS, grouped: core, tourism, and platform.

Core innovations
Multidisciplinary integrationGeology, archaeology and ecology in one exploration experience.
Cross-disciplinary interpretationAI finds relationships between disciplines instead of listing disconnected facts.
AI-powered hypothesesPossible links not yet documented, e.g. geology shaping ancient settlement — clearly separated from established findings.
Research democratisationPapers and technical reports become stories, visuals and interactive experiences.
Automated heritage discoveryCredible sources are monitored for newly documented sites, prepared for verification.
Interconnected knowledgeSimilarities between distant places, including across the six countries.
Space and time togetherGeography combined with geological time, archaeological chronology and environmental change.
Tourism innovations
Intelligent discoveryFind destinations by interest: geological wonders, ancient civilisations, living ecosystems.
Thematic journeysRoutes that connect places by a shared scientific, historical or environmental theme.
Context-aware recommendationsSuggestions by interest, location, time available and what each place offers.
Educational tourismDestinations become learning experiences for families, students and enthusiasts.
Hidden heritageOverlooked places that conventional tourism platforms do not highlight.
Platform and ecosystem
Living platformContent evolves as new research and verified information arrive.
Transparent validationPublished evidence, scientific interpretation and AI hypotheses are kept apart.
Citizen scienceVisitors, researchers and communities can contribute observations and finds.
One regional frameworkSix countries explored through a common geographical-heritage lens.
Visual storytellingInteractive maps, layers and timelines explain what text and photos cannot.
